index.p_what: Conquer is a turn-based fantasy strategy game for many players, first released on Usenet in 1987 by Ed Barlow and Adam Bryant. This server runs version 4.12 of the original game, now free software under the GPL. Each player rules a nation: build cities, raise armies, cast magic, trade and negotiate with other rulers, and expand across a shared world.
index.note_join: Joining takes three steps: ask for your seat, wait for the administrator to approve it, then found your nation inside the game.
index.join1: Ask for your seat: choose I want to play (under the buttons at the top), and pick an account name and a password. No email is asked. An invite link skips the wait.
index.join2: The administrator approves it. Nobody emails you: come back and press Play. Until then Play shows the practice world and the state of your seat. Your account is for this website only: it opens the door, and the sign-in page asks for it when you press Play.
index.join3: Your nation: press Play now and sign in with that account. The 1987 game asks you to found your nation: its own name (up to 9 letters), race, class and a nation password (2 to 7 characters). From then on, Play now opens it directly. If the game is already under way, your nation starts late, with extra points to catch up.
index.turns1: Log in as often as you like to give orders: move armies, draft troops, build, trade, send messages.
index.turns2: All orders are resolved together at the next turn update, on the schedule shown under Current game; the in-game menu shows it too, with the last update.
index.turns3: Before each update, players still in the game are warned and, a few minutes later, disconnected; their orders are saved. Press <kbd>q</kbd> to quit the game when you are done.
index.turns4: When you quit, the menu asks whether your orders for the turn are done. Once every nation is done, the update can run right away instead of waiting for the schedule.
index.before1: Conquer is controlled entirely with keys, so a computer keyboard is the most comfortable. On phones and tablets a touch layer lets you tap the map to move, and offers command chips for the current screen and a d-pad; sound is optional, in the options. Use the Keyboard button to type names and passwords.
index.before2: The game needs a terminal of at least 80×24 characters. If the menu warns that the screen is too small, enlarge the window or zoom out with Ctrl + -.
index.before3: If the screen looks garbled, press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>L</kbd> to redraw it.
index.before4: The game itself is in English.
index.footer: Conquer is free software (GPL-3.0-or-later). Source: game · web server

join.step1: A name and a password that open the door of the site: the sign-in page asks for them when you press Play, and can remember you for 30 days. It is not your nation: other players never see it.
join.step2: Once you are approved, the game asks you to found your nation: its name (up to 9 letters, it can differ from your account), race, class, and a nation password of 2 to 7 characters that the game asks for every time you play. At any turn: if the game is already under way, a late nation starts with extra points to catch up.

moves.title: How to move in Conquer
moves.sub: The letters sit under your right hand, and most point where they go: y u up, b n down, h left, l right. In the middle, j goes down (its tail hangs) and k up.
moves.why: Why letters? In 1987 many terminals had no arrow keys, so Conquer, like vi and rogue, moves with the letters under your right hand, and with the digits of the number pad. On this site the arrow keys work too; on a phone, the pad of the key bar.
moves.arrows: The number pad's digits work too and, on this site, the arrow keys.

story.title: The story of Conquer
story.hint: Tap or press Space to continue
story.d4: sahara changes status with darboth to WAR.
story.p1: Nineteen eighty-seven. In the computing centres of the universities, when everyone else had gone to sleep, the terminals stayed on.
story.p2: Two students, Ed Barlow and Adam Bryant, post a turn-based strategy game for many players on Usenet. There are no graphics: there is a world, drawn with letters.
story.p3: In that world there are four peoples. Men, who look into the future in a stone. Elves, who see it in the water. Dwarves, who carve it into the mountain. And orcs, who tear it out with iron.
story.p4: Each player gives their orders whenever they can. Once a day, the world moves on: armies march, harvests grow, treaties are kept or broken. And the newspaper tells it all.
story.p5: The universities changed their machines. The messages were lost. For thirty years, Conquer was the memory of a few.
story.p6: Until someone found it, asked its authors for permission, and brought it back into the light: the same game, the same code, free forever. Today the door opens again for anyone who speaks the word.
story.p7: Now it is your turn. Choose a people, name your nation, and take a corner of the world. The others are already here: allies you have yet to meet, and enemies who have already seen you.
story.p8: One turn a day. A whole lifetime of reign. Conquer.
